Question Choices: Which shows a smaller part of a whole 2/6 or 5/6?
Hints: For the same whole or equal-sized wholes, equal denominators mean equal-sized pieces. Compare the numerators.
Solution: Both fractions count sixths of the same whole. Since 2 < 5, 2/6 is smaller than 5/6.

Hints: For the same whole or equal-sized wholes, a larger positive denominator means smaller pieces. Compare the same positive number of those pieces.
Solution: Thirds are larger than fourths of the same whole. Two thirds is therefore larger than two fourths: 2/3 > 2/4.

Question Choices: A shape is divided into 15 equal parts. 3 parts are red, 5 other parts are blue, and the rest are not shaded. What fraction is NOT shaded?
Hints: Fractions = not shaded parts / total parts. 15 - (red + blue) = not shaded parts
Solution: The shaded parts total 3+5 = 8. The unshaded count is 15-8 = 7, so 7/15 is unshaded.

Hints: When the numerator is bigger than the denominator, the fraction is more than one whole.
Solution: Yes. One whole is 3/3 and 7 > 3, so 7/3 > 1.

Solution: Fifths are larger than ninths of the same whole. With 4 pieces in each fraction, 4/5 is larger than 4/9.
